name: Thang co
summary: The Hmong pot, and the accounts are not one recipe. Báo Sơn La, on 9 September 2025, names thắng cố for the Hmong, with a speaker in xã Co Mạ: men learn to cook it, women learn to mill mèn mén. No ingredient list is on that article. Vietnamnet, on 16 March 2019, places horse thắng cố on the Mộc Châu plateau and names 12 spices, including thảo quả, hoa hồi, quế chi, lemongrass, chili, ginger, and a last herb it calls cây thắng cố. Horse meat and offal are boiled, seasoned, then simmered for hours in horse-bone broth with offal and blood. Eat it with mèn mén, grilled corn cake, and rượu ngô.
origin: Báo Sơn La, 9 September 2025, xã Co Mạ. Vietnamnet, 16 March 2019, the Mộc Châu plateau.
taste: Vietnamnet calls the horse offal fragrant and a little crisp, with the heat of the greens and a chili dip. Báo Sơn La does not print a taste.
howToEat: From the pot. Vietnamnet adds a little chili, pepper, or salt, and dips cải mèo, cải ngồng, and other greens. The hour is Check on arrival. A price is Check on arrival.
where: Xã Co Mạ, on the 9 September 2025 naming. The horse pot Vietnamnet describes is on the Mộc Châu plateau, not a city street.
seoTitle: Thang co in Son La — Hmong pot, two accounts
seoDescription: Thắng cố in Sơn La. Báo Sơn La names it for the Hmong in xã Co Mạ and prints no recipe. Vietnamnet describes a horse pot on the Mộc Châu plateau. Check on arrival.
